context:
Extend registry metadata to carry support status and diagnostics while
preserving lazy optional imports. Generate public count claims from registry
metadata and give contributors a measured path for adding platforms.
description:
BenchBox's platform breadth is a strength, but the boundary between supported,
available, optional, experimental, repo-only, deprecated, and document-only is
blurry. Optional adapter import failures are intentionally swallowed to keep
base imports cheap, but missing dependencies and broken adapter imports are
hard to distinguish. Adding a new platform also touches many files and checks,
but that extension cost is not measured.

This item migrates the contract taxonomy into registry metadata, adds
diagnostics for optional imports, generates count tables from source of truth,
and creates a new-platform acceptance checklist/scaffold.

anti_patterns.dont: hand-edit README platform counts after this work
anti_patterns.why: generated or tested counts are the point

anti_patterns.instead: add diagnostics that can be requested.

anti_patterns.dont: treat an unavailable optional dependency as a broken adapter

deferrals.reason: Deletion should be separate unless the file is unambiguously dead and within scope.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Bulk 'delete every orphan file' needs per-file judgment per its own reason; the one concrete known case (cuDF) is already tracked separately.
deferrals.summary: Delete every orphan platform file found by inventory

deferrals.reason: Support status and diagnostics come first; full test-derived capability metadata is a larger design.

preserves.behavior: Do not conflate support_status with local dependency availability.
Do not make optional platform dependencies required for base import or docs generation.
Do not remove platform files in the same change unless they are explicitly classified and scoped.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/platform_registry.py: existing metadata source -- extend rather than creating a second platform catalogue.
benchbox/platforms/__init__.py: existing lazy optional adapter wiring -- preserve base import behavior.
docs/development/adding-new-platforms.md and adding-dataframe-platform.md: existing authoring guides -- turn into checklist/scaffold inputs.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -k 'platform_registry or optional import or support_status' --tb=short
verifications.description: Run focused platform registry and optional import tests.
verifications.expected: Registry metadata and diagnostic tests pass.

verifications.description: Run generated docs/check target for platform matrices.
verifications.expected: Docs drift checks pass or report only unrelated pre-existing issues.

verifications.description: Verify base import remains cheap and optional.

work_units.notes:
Completed 2026-05-21 at checked SHA ed9db3c8dbc03a01987ed97db714aee3049c71ed.

Revalidation summary:
  - `PlatformRegistry.get_all_platform_metadata()` exposed 50 metadata
    entries: 45 SQL-capable, 19 DataFrame-capable, 14 dual-mode, and
    5 DataFrame-only.
  - `README.md` no longer had stale platform counts, while
    `docs/platforms/comparison-matrix.md` still claimed 41 platforms
    and 30 SQL + 11 DataFrame.
  - `_try_register_adapter()` and `benchbox/platforms/__init__.py`
    intentionally swallowed optional import failures but did not expose a
    diagnostic split between missing SDKs, native load failures, broken
    adapter imports, or deprecated selectors.
  - Recent platform additions showed a minimum durable extension cost of
    4 files for small follow-ups and 7-12 files for normal SQL/DataFrame
    additions once registry metadata, docs, dependencies, tests, and
    compatibility/UAT scope are included.
  - File inventory found `benchbox/platforms/cudf.py` as a legacy
    top-level module importing `benchbox.experimental.gpu`; removal was
    deferred to a follow-up TODO.

Commit a compact summary of checked SHA, registry platform counts,
SQL/DataFrame capability counts, docs counts, optional import behavior,
and files touched by recent platform additions.

Minimum evidence to re-check:
  - benchbox/core/platform_registry.py metadata and _try_register_adapter.
  - benchbox/platforms/__init__.py optional adapter wiring.
  - README.md platform counts.
  - docs/platforms/comparison-matrix.md counts.
  - docs/development/adding-new-platforms.md.
  - docs/development/adding-dataframe-platform.md.
work_units.summary: Revalidate registry counts, docs counts, optional import behavior, and platform-add docs

work_units.notes:
Use the taxonomy from architecture-contract-map-and-support-taxonomy:
stable, beta, experimental, repo_only, deprecated, document_only. Add
validation so every registry platform has exactly one support_status and
docs can render it.

Do not confuse dependency availability with support status. A stable
platform can be unavailable locally because an optional dependency is not
installed.
work_units.summary: Add support_status to platform metadata using the accepted taxonomy

work_units.notes:
Keep normal imports lazy and quiet for missing optional dependencies, but
add a diagnostic mode or command that reports:
  - missing optional dependency,
  - native library/load failure,
  - broken adapter import bug,
  - intentionally disabled/deprecated platform.

Do not make base benchbox import fail because an optional platform is
broken.
work_units.summary: Add diagnostic mode for optional adapter import failures

work_units.notes:
Replace hand-maintained platform count claims where feasible. Generated
tables should include support_status, SQL/DataFrame capability, dependency
group, and whether the platform is exposed in CLI/MCP/docs.

Add a docs drift check so README and comparison matrix counts cannot
disagree with platform registry metadata silently. Benchmark count and
benchmark support-status ownership stays with the benchmark API follow-up
because benchmark metadata lives in `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py`.
work_units.summary: Generate platform count and support-status tables from registry metadata

work_units.notes:
The checklist must cover SQL and DataFrame platforms separately:
  - adapter/family/context files,
  - registry metadata and support_status,
  - optional dependency extras,
  - SQL compatibility rules or explicit exemptions,
  - docs and generated platform matrix updates,
  - fast/unit/platform smoke tests,
  - UAT/live scope where relevant,
  - deprecation/retirement expectations.
work_units.summary: Create a new-platform acceptance checklist covering files, tests, docs, compat, and UAT

work_units.notes:
Add either a small scaffold script or documented template set. Track
"files touched to add one platform" as an architecture health metric and
include a before/after number based on a recent platform addition.

The scaffold should be optional helper tooling, not a new framework that
platform authors must fight.
work_units.summary: Add a platform scaffold or template and measure extension cost

work_units.notes:
Identify orphan platform files, especially dead paths that import
experimental modules. Classify each as supported, deprecated,
experimental, repo-only, or removal candidate. Create follow-up TODOs for
removal if deletion is outside this item's scope.
work_units.summary: Inventory orphan/deprecated platform files and classify them
